decisions.rationale: Accept: the options were signature shorthand presented as methods. The bounded correction labels them as signatures with return types and bodies omitted; the education delta recheck at 1d1dc3be resolved it and later reviews retain those bytes by exact identity.

Accept: o2 omitted ordinary and invalid inputs and result checking. One boundary item was replaced with a balanced test-set item with expected results; the education delta recheck at 1d1dc3be resolved it and later reviews retain those bytes by exact identity.

Accept: the credited and wraparound feedback contradicted each other. The credited feedback now says the base case is not reached before the stack is exhausted; the education rechecks at 31cfc9a5 and f7739257 confirm it remains resolved.

Accept: the unbounded stem let Step Over also satisfy it. The stem now says no breakpoint is set inside helper and asks which control directly enters it; the education rechecks at 31cfc9a5 and f7739257 confirm it remains resolved.

Accept: JLS SE 25 8.4.7 requires a return only on paths that can complete normally. The feedback was qualified accordingly; the Java recheck at 31cfc9a5 resolved it and f7739257 retains the bytes by exact identity.

Accept: the bare-name distractor was context-dependent and the no-object rationale was inaccurate. The scenario is bounded to an unrelated class without inheritance or static import and names the missing Player receiver; the Java recheck at 31cfc9a5 resolved it.

Accept: the growing-String scenario had no unique resource-exhaustion answer. It was replaced with an int count(n + 1) scenario, and the permitted-stack assumption added for TECH-FINAL-RECHECK-01 makes StackOverflowError the unique key; the final Java recheck at f7739257 approves it.
Accept: Step Over can stop at enabled breakpoints in called methods. The feedback now states that caveat; the Java recheck at 31cfc9a5 confirmed the correction and f7739257 approves the bank.

Accept: the earlier universal stack-exhaustion claim was technically unsupported because Java int wraparound can reach zero absent a resource bound. The explicit permitted-stack assumption at f7739257 is the smallest intent-preserving correction, and the final Java recheck resolves it.
Accept: Resume has no caller-specific stop and may next break in the caller. The corrected feedback at f7739257 is accurate, and the final Java recheck resolves it.
